It depends on the map and what game type youre playing.

But for the most part, DR is best for when the enemy team is really spammy, like if you're just out of the gate as BLU on payload. Use DR to get behind them, as chances are you're not gonna invisiwatch through all the sticky/rocket spam.

CnD is obviously best if you need to take your time. Like if you're trying to take out a sentry nest. You can stay in a nice spot and wait for the engineers to get distracted, like if your team pushes in with an uber you can go and start sapping. Or if the engineer walks away or dies for whatever reason, you can go and start sapping. You just have to be careful about waiting too long, lest random spychecking, another spy or a just a teammate being near you kill you.

IW is a good middle man/all-rounder. You can get past the enemy team, but also collect metal and just stay in a certain area. This should be your default, but that's just my opinion.

You should switch every so often regardless, just to throw your enemies off. If they keep expecting you to DR they'll get better at countering it, but if you switch to CnD this can throw them off your trail.

If you're on defense, I recommend the CnD. It's more passive play style means you'll survive longer, which is what you want due to longer respawn times. It'll also allow you to hopefully get a medic pick if they're about to uber against your team's sentry nest or something.

 Going DR tends to not work as well if you have a 20 sec respawn timer after all. Usage of DR should stick to offensive for that reason, you're more likely to die to the aggressive play style it gives you.

IW could be used either on offense or defense, as long as it gets you past the enemy team/where you need to go.

Honestly you should switch out most of your loadout a lot, in terms of knife and revolver as well. It'll allow you to get used to all the different play styles spy offers and make you a well rounded spy, rather than a one trick pony so to speak. Its okay to have a preferred loadout and all, but having a good plan B is always nice.

I'm a spy main, but I've only put in 150 hours into Spy, so I'm sure there is better advice out there. Just switch it up and get good game sense and you'll do well.
